The three branches share merge-base 9317d6700260f05ed657839edf0b592a3d16f7a0 (condensed into 8251007). Treat that improvements snapshot as the implementation baseline, incorporate its later seven commits, then finish the two sibling branches. Neither sibling is ready as-is.

Confirmed source defects to fix

  1. NumPy cluster scattering bypasses the coincident-particle check. Cluster.solve() rejects coincident particles, but Cluster.factor()/scatter() build the generic expansion directly; that expansion treats coincident particles as zero self-coupling and can return a finite, physically invalid response. The framework branch guards only its own scattering route.

    Evidence: 50058abd:python/treams_rs/_cluster.py:159-186 (condensed into ae22657); _tmatrix.py:483-491; crates/treams-core/src/sw/expansion.rs:224-233; native rejection in cluster/particles.rs:96-102.

    Proposed default: enforce the particle-geometry invariant consistently across NumPy solve/factor/scatter and framework solve/scatter, preserving legitimate self-block handling inside generic expansion. Verify identical rejected geometry and valid sphere/cylinder results across these routes.

  2. The framework achirality fix misses outgoing port waves. PortWave.with_polarization("parity") copies the wave and converts its coefficients without checking its medium. A wave scattered into a chiral exterior can therefore enter parity and evaluate fields, despite the new TMatrix/Wave/SMatrix checks and documented invariant.

    Evidence: 50058abd:python/treams_rs/_framework_waves.py:402-455 (condensed into ae22657); field evaluation at :474-481; corresponding checked NumPy construction at _waves.py:139-140.

    Proposed default: complete the existing shared achirality enforcement, covering static and traced chirality through Advect, JAX and Torch. The new tests at tests/autodiff/test_framework_physics.py:845-905 do not exercise this port-wave conversion.

Known unfinished branch work

Branch Required completion
Threading 9e98d507 (condensed into ae22657) Recover handoff/memory-error.patch and handoff/ordered-reductions-wip.patch; they are embedded text, not landed implementation. Finish deterministic pullback reductions, resolve known Clippy/reproducibility failures, regenerate docs, qualify the combined Python/native paths, then delete handoff/.
Framework 50058abd (condensed into ae22657) Complete full CI/docs checks and the stopped adversarial review; repair the two invariant gaps above; obtain trustworthy targeted timing; remove HANDOFF.md.
Improvements 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007) Preserve later fixes and Dependabot, and qualify the final integrated numerical source rather than relying on old recorded results. Resolve the numerical contract boundaries below.

Threading evidence is explicit: 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:3-15,85-174 (condensed into ae22657). It historically reports both patches together passing formatting, Clippy and 235 Rust tests, while leaving Python tests, generated docs and wheel checks undone (:144-154). These results were not rerun.

The allocation guarantee needs narrowing or completion: even its patch leaves infallible allocations in matrix products, SVD/eigenvalue workspaces, periodic tables and binding input copies (handoff/README.md:113-116; crates/treams-py/src/convert.rs:305-314). Public docs currently promise more generally that refused allocations become MemoryError (docs/design/parallelism.md:113-123). Finish consequential supported paths or describe the actual coverage; two Linux RLIMIT_AS examples do not establish a universal guarantee.

Ordered reductions retain up to 64 complete partial gradients (numerics/parallel.rs:120,154-159). Check representative large field/cluster gradient peak memory as well as bitwise reproducibility. Sequential SVD/eigendecomposition, current parallel cutoffs and GIL-enabled configuration can remain; parallel decompositions and further scheduling optimizations are optional work.

Numerical decisions to resolve before shipping

These are documented limitations or handoff reports, not newly reproduced numerical failures.

  • Negative-real spherical Ewald wavenumbers: documentation explicitly admits results of another function, while the shared boundary accepts them. Reference tests exclude this region. Default: reject unsupported spherical Ewald inputs centrally while preserving supported cylindrical and direct-shell paths. Evidence: 1f8b6077:docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:133-150 (condensed into 8251007); crates/treams-core/src/lattice/mod.rs:437-454; tests/lattice/test_lattice.py:928-934.
  • Field evaluation depends on length-unit scaling in an extreme documented case: degree-40 singular spherical fields at radius 1e-7 can become NaN because the kernel forms z_l(kr)/r^l before multiplying dimensional solid harmonics. Default: qualify equivalent dimensionless geometries in metres, micrometres and normalized units; correct intermediate scaling, or fail explicitly at the unsupported boundary. Evidence: 1f8b6077:docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:56-57 (condensed into 8251007); crates/treams-core/src/fields.rs:139-159,191-208,449-475.
  • Partial-polarization slabs: NumPy composes projections at every interface, while the framework computes the complete two-polarization response and projects afterward. That source divergence is confirmed; the handoff’s reported 0.944 versus 0.917 transmitted power remains unverified. Default: establish one supported physical contract across both APIs, or explicitly constrain partial-port constructions before release. Evidence: 50058abd:python/treams_rs/_smatrix.py:590-608 (condensed into ae22657); _framework.py:408-433; HANDOFF.md:168-179.
  • Gain media / strong chirality: NumPy’s xy interface uses closed-form Fresnel blocks while framework interfaces and full slabs use layer_stack. The handoff reports order-one disagreement for gain and κ exceeding Re(n), but does not reverify it. Default: reproduce the cases against an independent physical reference; resolve equivalence or reject unsupported combinations. Do not choose a branch solely to match another implementation. Evidence: _smatrix.py:440-452; _framework.py:408-419; HANDOFF.md:175-179.
  • Gain-media lattice claims: documentation admits split dependence and branch jumps for some Im(k)<0 cases, while diff.lattice_sum broadly describes full sums as independent of the split. Reconcile the supported contract and wording. Evidence: 1f8b6077:docs/validation/numerical-limits.md:137-150 (condensed into 8251007); python/treams_rs/diff.py:361-363.

Existing explicit limits—CPU execution, first-order differentiation, singular diffraction thresholds, bounded conditioning/order domains and unsupported fractional-complex Legendre functions—need not become implementation projects for the first release.

Integration and validation

Source overlaps, without a merge simulation:

  • Framework versus threading: CHANGELOG.md, docs/development/benchmarks.md.
  • Later improvements versus threading: CHANGELOG.md, tests/api/test_namespaces.py.
  • Later improvements versus framework: CHANGELOG.md.
  • Embedded threading patches both modify fields.rs imports; their intended reconciliation is recorded at handoff/README.md:146-149.

Require a fresh integrated extension and actual wheel, full physical/reference/gradient suites, all advertised adapters and independent-reference dependencies installed, and release-supported CPython 3.12–3.15. Dependency-based skips otherwise allow apparently green runs without the intended numerical evidence. Historical qualification binds a different commit (benchmarks/linux-core-qualification.json:5), not the final integration.

For threading, verify one and multiple threads; every public pullback in the reproducibility tests; fork/forkserver/spawn after prior native work; context restoration, threadpoolctl, ufunc reductions and floating-point mode; then the allocation subprocess cases and representative gradient RSS.

Keep performance work bounded: rerun changed framework calls with unchanged NumPy controls on an idle host, plus the previously identified eight timing gates after integration stabilizes. The framework’s reported 15–27% small Advect parity slowdown is noisy evidence, not yet a confirmed regression (HANDOFF.md:117-149). Finish the new comparator’s known Torch detach warning; ensure worker failures clean up every child—its current cleanup loop can stop when the first Worker.close() raises (scripts/compare_builds.py:473-495).

No broad placeholder-code cleanup emerged: the inspected improvements core/Python/tests contain no TODO/FIXME/todo!/unimplemented!/xfail matches. Keep the deliberately ignored Rust subprocess-child tests and legitimate platform skips.

This was a targeted source audit, including the complete framework delta and delegated threading/numerical-boundary inspection, not exhaustive scientific certification of the large improvements branch. No edits, checkouts, tests, builds, commits, pushes, PR changes or remote mutations were performed.
